5. The learned Advocate further submits that on investigation charge sheet was submitted on 20-4-2008 which was also found to be violative of Rules 7 and 10 of the ACC Rules, 2007. Even the learned Senior Special judge, Dhaka did not obtain "sanction" as required under section 32(1) of the ACC Ain, 2004 read with Rule 15(7) of the ACC Rules, 2007. The learned Advocate has further urged that the "sanction" required under section 32(1) of the ACC Act is to be accorded by "Commission" as defined under section. 2(Ka) of the Ain, 2004, not by any member of the said Commission. Moreover, the alleged "sanction" annexed with the police report is merely a "mechanical sanction" which in the eye of law is no "sanction", at all, and is quite insufficient to prosecute any person for commission of the schedule offence, noted above. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred a decision of the case of Abdul Hakim vs State reported in 45 DLR 352. The learned Advocate further submits that the period for commission of the alleged offence as has been shown in the FIR "since 1971 to 10-6-2007" also stands against the provision as laid down in section 234 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as such, the framing of charge for commission of offence alleged to have been committed within the period of more than one year punishable' under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Ain, 2004 is absolutely illegal and liable to be quashed. Moreover, trial of the case has not also been concluded within the prescribed period of 60 days as contemplated i!l section 6A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, on that score as well, the impugned proceeding is liable to be quashed. 

 9. As to the question of violation of section 234 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2 has candidly argued that by incorporating section 6(1B) in the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (vide Order No. VI of 1979) the legislature has ousted the application of the said provision in view of section 6(1) of the said Act of 1958. Accordingly, he submits that since the accused-petitioner has miserably failed to substantiate any of the grounds so resorted to the Rule should be discharged. 

 13. Now, let us examine whether the provisions laid down in Rule 10 of the ACC Rules, 2007 and section 6A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 so far it relates to the prescribed period of investigation and trial respectively has been complied with or not. Opposite-party No. 2 by filing counter-affidavit has given the account in details about the time, consumed for investigation, where 59 "working days" are found to have been exhausted for the purpose of investigation of the instant case. In spite of that, we also feel it urgent to decide whether the provisions laid down in Rule 10 of the ACC Rules, 2007 and 6A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is mandatory or directory. 

 14. Rule 10 of ACC Rules 2007 and section 6A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 are quoted below: 

 16. With this view in mind we are of opinion that since consequence has not been given under Rule 10 of the ACC Rules, 2007 or section 6A of the Act, 1958 in case of failure to oblige the "time-limit" as such the accused cannot derive any benefit out of it. In support of this view, we may safely rely upon the decision of the case reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 11. 

 17. Now, let us examine whether "sanction" for prosecution as required under section 32(1) of the ACC Ain 2004 has been given or not. No doubt "sanction" as required under the said provision of law is precondition for taking cognizance of the offence as described in the schedule of the Ain but we cannot accept this view in the light of the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that this sanction is not a sanction in the eye of law since no reason has been assigned for its satisfaction. In fact, this decision referred to above by the learned Advocate for the petitioner was based on section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 where State was the prosecution and that no format like that of "Form 3" of the ACC Rules, 2007 was ever incorporated therein. But with the promulgation of the Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004 the entire scheme of the prosecution has been changed. The new Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004 has provided new Rules in order to regulate sanction or other stage of the enquiry and trial of the case. 

 24. Now, let us see whether on the face of the provision laid down in section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 incorporated in the year 1979 the provision of section 234, the Code of Criminal Procedure is applicable or not. 

 26. The period of one year is available in section 234 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but it is absent in section 6 (lB) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act and thereby in view of the provision laid down in section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 section 6(1 B) excludes' the application of section 234 which relates to the period of the commission of the alleged offence.
